newsitem.title: COMOROS: Comoros agrees to economic surveillance.
newsitem.headline: Comoros agrees to economic surveillance.

text.p: The Comoros government, the World Bank and the International Monetary Fund agreed on a six months' surveillance programme to oversee an expenditure cut in the cash-strapped Indian Ocean islands, officials said on Sunday.
For months, the Comoros has been hit by a succession of strikes by civil servants complaining they had not been paid.

The new programme, decided on Saturday, involves cutting the annual government payroll from $26 million to $22 million, privatising ailing state-owned companies and increasing customs duties and taxes, officials said.
An unspecified number of civil servants will be laid off despite the risk of boosting unrest in the islands, the officials said.

State radio quoted Finance Minister Mohamed Ali Soilihi as saying the Comoros government had in the past failed to abide by undertakings to cut spending. For this reason, the World Bank and the IMF would monitor the islands' economy closely for a six-month period.
